subject: Banking
title: Barings Bank: The Rogue Trader
description: A short lesson to help you apply Barings Bank: The Rogue Trader.

hook.text: Nick Leeson was a 28-year-old trader who single-handedly destroyed Britain's oldest merchant bank. Barings fell in 1995.

buildup.text: Leeson was supposed to make safe arbitrage trades in Singapore. Instead he made massive bets on Japanese stock futures.

discovery.text: He hid losses in a secret account numbered 88888. By the time anyone found out, losses exceeded $1.3 billion.

twist.text: Barings had survived 233 years, financed wars, and served the Queen. One trader in a back office wiped it all out.

climax.text: Barings' failure proved that internal controls matter more than reputation.

punchline.text: 233-year-old bank. One rogue trader. $1.3 billion in hidden losses. Gone.

quiz.question: How did Nick Leeson hide his trading losses?

details.summary: Barings Bank, Britain's oldest merchant bank founded in 1762, was destroyed in 1995 by a single trader, Nick Leeson, who hid $1.4 billion in unauthorized losses in a secret account from his Singapore office.
details.whyItMatters: A 233-year-old institution was wiped out by one employee exploiting basic control failures. Barings proved that even the most prestigious banks can collapse from internal weaknesses.
takeaways: Leeson controlled both trading and back-office settlement at Barings Singapore
Losses were hidden in a secret account numbered 88888
Barings was sold to ING for one British pound after its collapse

faq.question: How did one trader destroy a 233-year-old bank?
faq.answer: Leeson held dual roles controlling both trading and settlement, allowing him to hide losses. Management trusted his reported profits and never independently verified his positions. When losses exceeded the bank's entire capital, there was nothing left.

faq.question: What banking reforms followed the Barings collapse?
faq.answer: The failure led to mandatory separation of trading and settlement functions, stronger internal audit requirements, and independent risk management oversight. It became a foundational case study in operational risk management.
